summary.headline: Rico Auto FY26 consolidated revenue hit record INR2,477 crore (+12% YoY); Q4 EBITDA margin fell to 7.1% on INR14.6 crore one-offs.
summary.overview: Management reported record FY26 revenue of INR2,477 crore, up 12% YoY, with EBITDA of INR223 crore (9% margin) and PAT of INR52.4 crore versus INR19.2 crore last year. Q4 was weaker: revenue INR677 crore, EBITDA INR47.8 crore (7.1% margin), PAT INR6.9 crore, with a Labour Code charge (INR3.6 crore) and raw-material lag settlement loss (INR11 crore) hitting the quarter. Management says the adjusted FY26 EBITDA margin was 10.25% and expects FY27 margins above that, with monthly raw-material settlements agreed by 75% of customers by value. Railway and defence scale-up, Hosur capacity from September 2026, and a INR2,500 crore five-year order win were highlighted as growth drivers.

financial_highlights.change: Management also cited 7.6% on one slide-equivalent basis in Q&A; adjusted for one-offs ~9.8%

segments.name: Aluminium
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR2,155 crore, about 88% of total. Small-tonnage die-casting machines run near 95% utilisation; higher-tonnage machines have spare capacity.

segments.name: Ferrous
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR322 crore, about 12% of total. Capacity utilisation around 65-75% as of Q4.

segments.name: Railways
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue only INR3-4 crore. RDSO approval received for some assemblies; first lot dispatched around late May 2026. Internal FY27 target above INR100 crore.

segments.name: Defence
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue around INR20-30 crore. FY27 target above INR50 crore, with plans to double in the following two years.

segments.name: Machine tools (CNC)
segments.commentary: Company-built CNC machines (5, 8, 14 and 16 axis) previously used in-house; first external sale just completed. No sales figure given yet; to be shared next quarter.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue expected to cross INR3,000 crore (about 20%+ growth), per CFO; budget still being finalised.
FY27 EBITDA margin expected above the 10.25% adjusted FY26 level, if other factors hold; management said 10%+ margin achievable from Q1 FY27.
Exports to US and Germany expected to grow about 32% this year and double in two years.
Net debt repayments of about INR110-120 crore a year over next three years; leverage cited at about 3.75x.
Industry FY27 growth guidance: passenger vehicles 5-7%, 2-wheelers 6-8%, commercial vehicles 4-6%, 3-wheelers 9-10%.
Railway and defence margins expected to be better than auto margins; detail deferred 1-2 quarters.
capex_capacity: Hosur facility expected to become operational from September 2026, mainly for hybrid and EV programmes for key OEMs.
Tamil Nadu government approved subsidy of about INR39 crore, accruing from current FY and available for 10 years.
New orders worth about INR2,500 crore over five-year programme life; management said ramp-up begins this year and peaks next year, with about 40 product launches underway.
Ferrous capacity utilisation about 65-75%; aluminium small machines near 95%, large machines have freed capacity.
Company owns surplus land at its plant; earlier INR700 crore offer rejected, talks ongoing for a better price, sale only if right price achieved (may be done within 6 months).
demand_pricing: Raw material (aluminium) prices volatile; customer pass-through limited margin impact in FY26, but quarterly RM settlements created a lag loss of INR19 crore for FY26 (INR11 crore in Q4).
Negotiating with customers to move RM settlement from quarterly to monthly; 75% of customers by value have agreed.
Separate negotiation under way to recover FY26 lag losses; any recovery flows directly to bottom line.
Reviewing portfolio to identify low-margin products and renegotiating prices; also seeking pass-through of non-RM conversion cost inflation and imported consumables/energy costs.
Order pipeline cited with Toyota, Maruti Suzuki, Hero, Bosch, Cummins and Knorr-Bremse across transmission, braking, engine and EV applications.
Company describes itself as single-source supplier on current programmes; growth expected from share gains and hybrid/EV components rather than just market growth.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 EBITDA margin and gross margin decline sharply, and what is FY27 margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO attributed Q4 to INR3.6 crore Labour Code impact and INR11 crore RM lag settlement; adjusted Q4 margin about 9.8%. FY26 adjusted margin 10.25% vs ~9%, with FY27 expected higher.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR11 crore Q4 / INR19 crore FY26 lag loss recoverable and will it be in FY27 profit?
qa_highlights.answer: Monthly settlements are agreed for future price moves; recovery of past losses is under negotiation separately, and any amount recovered adds to margin.

qa_highlights.question: What is railway and defence revenue in FY26 and what products?
qa_highlights.answer: Railway about INR3-4 crore in FY26, target above INR100 crore in FY27; defence INR20-30 crore, target above INR50 crore. Railway products include bearing adapters, cast iron inserts, track adjusters and distance blocks; 3-4 of 7-8 assemblies approved, balance expected in about 2 months.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the earlier INR60-70 crore railway and defence target for FY26 missed?
qa_highlights.answer: Production was ready but RDSO and customer approvals took longer; approvals now in place for about 5-6 assembly types.

qa_highlights.question: How can revenue grow 20%+ when OEM volumes grow under 10%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited 40 product launches from investments made 1-2 years earlier, single-source positions, share gains and new hybrid/EV components, with impact from end Q3 to Q4 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What are current capacity utilisation levels?
qa_highlights.answer: Ferrous around 65-75%; aluminium similar overall, with small machines near 95% and high-tonnage machines having free capacity.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook on net debt and leverage?
qa_highlights.answer: Leverage about 3.75x; scheduled repayments about INR110-120 crore a year over next three years, with a downward path expected.

risks_watch: Recovery of FY26 raw-material lag losses (INR19 crore) is still under negotiation; outcome not assured.
Q4 FY26 PAT fell to INR6.9 crore despite record annual revenue; sustainability of 10%+ margin from Q1 FY27 depends on customer renegotiations.
Railway and defence remain small (FY26 under INR35 crore combined) and rely on approvals; targets missed once already.
Hosur plant start-up (September 2026) and ramp of INR2,500 crore order book are execution-dependent.
Geopolitical and commodity (aluminium, imported consumables, energy) cost volatility.
Surplus land sale timing and price uncertain.
Management's Q&A figures have minor inconsistencies (Q4 margin cited as 7.1% and 7.6%; Q4 revenue described as FY25 in prepared remarks) and should be checked against the filed financial results.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term growth, railway/defence and the FY27 margin path, but cautious and hedged on specifics (settlement recoveries, defence timelines, exact railway margins). Management frequently qualified forecasts with "if everything else remains as it is" and "unless geopolitics disrupts."

So if you exclude this onetime impact, the margin increases from 9-odd percent to 10.25%.
So we should see the kind of margin going forward starting from Q1 itself.
If it happens, it will happen in 6 months also. If it doesn't happen -- If we don't get the right price, we are not selling it.

growth.why: Management guides FY27 revenue above INR3,000 crore (about 20%+ growth), backed by a ~INR2,500 crore five-year order win with ramp-up starting this year, Hosur capacity from September 2026, and railway/defence scale-up; budget is still being finalised and no order-level timing or revenue split was given for the total.
